case_design: Fresh ordinary Edge sessions, one mobile Yes, a separate desktop No, and a physical through-lane tap with passenger-initiated alternative-bay lookup. Each image response on the page was hashed against its previously published original.

pickup.request: Could you drop me next to that black pickup truck?

before.title: Is this the vehicle you meant?
before.message: I can see a black truck left of centre in the photo. I couldn’t verify that it is a pickup. Is that the vehicle you meant? I haven’t verified an open space beside it.

after_yes.title: I found the vehicle you described
after_yes.message: You confirmed the outlined vehicle. Please mark the open ground beside it where you want to get out. I’ll check that spot on the photo.

after_no.title: Which spot do you mean?
after_no.message: Which vehicle did you mean? Describe its colour, body type or position in the photo, or mark the spot where you want to get out.

after_tap.title: Choose another location
after_tap.message: That point appears to be in a traffic lane. Could you mark a visible parking bay instead?

after_request.title: Which parking bay do you mean?
after_request.message: More than one bay matches your description. Choose bay A or bay B.

after_b.title: Is this your intended bay?
after_b.message: The gold ring marks the centre of the outlined parking bay in the bottom centre of the photo.

after_explicit_save.title: Location saved
after_explicit_save.message: You chose the outlined parking bay as your intended drop-off. The gold ring marks its centre.

scope: Known public-gallery regressions. The parking choices are separate from the rejected traffic-lane mark. Confirming the possible vehicle never approves stopping.
